beats.narration: Module five — the last one. Your builds work: a production agent, a hardened Claude Code setup, MCP connections that pass review. This module is about what happens after a build works. You either rebuild it from scratch on the next engagement, or you package it once and the next team just configures it. The second path is this whole module.

beats.narration: Five abilities by the end. Package a working solution as an accelerator — a parameterized template, a configurable MCP server, or a portable eval suite. Contribute assets back through channels a maintainer can accept. Choose where a workload runs — the first-party API, Amazon Bedrock, or Google Vertex — and version what ships. Compare platforms on latency, compliance, and cost, well enough for procurement to sign off. And coordinate several deployments in one workflow without breaking a trust boundary.

items.text: 3. choose the platform + version what ships

beats.narration: One recurring gap runs through it all: a build that works is not yet a build that survives reuse, review, or deployment. The template must configure for a team that never spoke to you. The contribution must verify without reconstruction. The model must be pinned, so an upstream change is a decision instead of a surprise. The platform must clear residency and compliance. The point where code starts working is where this module's work begins.
